raw_notes: Susan Chartuse is an 11-year-old 5th grade student at Orange Sables Elementary referred for evaluation due to parental concerns regarding possible ADHD and dyslexia. Background history notes early developmental milestones were met at an average rate, with a history of chronic ear infections, tonsillectomy at age eight, and early physical high activity. She was retained in kindergarten. In school, she struggles with reading and math, but excels in creative writing. Behavioral observations during testing revealed a habit of mentally drifting when tasks became challenging, easy discouragement, and decoding issues during reading tasks. Comprehensive testing included the WISC-V, Woodcock-Johnson IV Tests of Cognitive Ability, Oral Language, and Achievement, Conners Parent Rating Scale, Achenbach CBCL, and IVA Continuous Performance Test. Results on the WISC-V revealed a Full Scale IQ of 98 (Average range), with a significant discrepancy between her Verbal Comprehension Index (VCI = 78, Very Low) and Fluid Reasoning Index (FRI = 118, High Average). WJ-IV Achievement testing placed her Broad Reading at grade equivalent 3.1 (percentile rank 7) and Broad Mathematics at grade equivalent 3.5 (percentile rank 5), indicating deficits approximately 2 to 2.5 grade levels behind her placement. Visual processing deficits (Number-Pattern Matching percentile 19) support a diagnosis of dyslexia, while auditory processing and memory functions remain relative strengths. Parent rating scales (Conners T-score 87 for executive functioning, 88 for hyperactivity/impulsivity; CBCL clinical elevation in inattention) and clinical observation support an ADHD diagnosis despite a passing IVA score. Formal DSM-5 diagnoses provided by Dr. Gary M. Eisenberg include Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder - Combined Type, Learning Disorder with impairments in reading, and Learning Disorder with impairments in mathematics. Recommendations include discussing psychostimulant medication with her pediatrician, daily exercise, participation in enjoyable extracurriculars, maintaining self-esteem, and specific IEP accommodations including extra movement breaks during tests, extended test time (1.5x), and testing in a quiet, solitary environment, alongside active reading comprehension strategies like SQR3.
academic_history: Susan was retained in kindergarten. By third grade, she had difficulty with multiplication tables, telling time, and coin values. Current testing places her broad reading at 3.1 grade equivalent and broad mathematics at 3.5 grade equivalent.
teacher_observations: Preschool teachers noted she would wander off during class, and first-grade teachers reported she could not sit in her seat. During testing, she mentally drifted when work became difficult but was responsive to redirection.
parent_concerns: Parents were concerned that Susan may have ADHD or dyslexia, noted difficulty pronouncing words, and reported focus issues delaying homework completion.
disability_category_raw: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder – Combined Type, Learning Disorder with impairments in reading, Learning Disorder with impairments in mathematics
